conflicts.why: Next.js, Remix, and similar routers require a default export on page and layout modules. Resolving modules.default-export to TS-ENTRY-001 turns the named-export ban off for every file. Keep both methodologies: TS-DEFAULT-001 excludes pages/** and app/**/page and layout files by default, so the ban still applies everywhere else and TS-ENTRY-001 still requires a default export on those entries. An override that replaces that exclude must keep the entry globs.

relations.why: Nuxt loads server routes, middleware and plugins from their default export (export default defineEventHandler(...)).
relations.settle: Exclude server/**, middleware/**, plugins/** and nuxt.config.ts from TS-DEFAULT-001.

relations.why: Expo Router loads screens and layouts under app/ from their default export.
relations.settle: Exclude the app/** route files from TS-DEFAULT-001 and keep named exports for components and modules elsewhere.

source.work: Google TypeScript style and Airbnb JavaScript style
source.paraphrase: Prefer named exports so the binding has one name at the definition and at the import.

invariants.why: A default export is renamed by every importer, so a search for the function's name misses call sites.
invariants.fixHint: Export the function or class by name. Page and layout entries are excluded by default; enable typescript/framework-entries to require their default export.
invariants.avoid: export { Page as default } is a default export. A comment that contains the words export default is not one. exports.default = Page is an assignment, not this syntax, and is a hole.
